CVE-1999-0001.d: ip_input.c in BSD-derived TCP/IP implementations allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash or hang) via crafted packets.

CVE-1999-0073.d: Telnet allows a remote client to specify environment variables including LD_LIBRARY_PATH, allowing an attacker to bypass the normal system libraries and gain root access.

CVE-1999-0517.d: An SNMP community name is the default (e.g. public), null, or missing.

CVE-1999-0524.d: ICMP information such as (1) netmask and (2) timestamp is allowed from arbitrary hosts.

CVE-1999-0532.d: A DNS server allows zone transfers.

CVE-1999-0678.d: A default configuration of Apache on Debian GNU/Linux sets the ServerRoot to /usr/doc, which allows remote users to read documentation files for the entire server.

CVE-1999-1053.d: guestbook.pl cleanses user-inserted SSI commands by removing text between "<!--" and "-->" separators, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands when guestbook.pl is run on Apache 1.3.9 and possibly other versions, since Apache allows other closing sequences besides "-->".
